newsitem.title: ITALY: EU faces logjam on IGC Commission reform.
newsitem.headline: EU faces logjam on IGC Commission reform.

text.p: The European Union headed for another logjam in the inter-governmental conference on Tuesday as France insisted that the number of European commissioners should be cut by half.

Without such a cut, French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said, Paris would not agree to give up one of its two commissioners, a move seen as essential if the EU executive is to be made sleeker as the bloc expand eastwards.
"We would never accept that," de Charette said, repeating the French position that there should be no more than 10 commissioners.
EU treaty negotiators have been struggling to find a way to limit the number of commissioners in order not to create a bureaucratic monster when a wave of new states join in the next decade or so.
There are now 20 commissioners, one for each country and a second for France, Germany, Britain, Italy and Spain.

The Commission itself has recommended that its numbers be capped at 20, with each country having no more than one commissioner. If the bloc moves beyond 20 countries, it says, that is the time to think again.
Most of the bloc's large countries are willing to give up their second commissioner, while the small member states are happy with the proposal because it protects their right to a commissioner.
Anything less than 20 would be too difficult for the small states, German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said, adding that he would otherwise be happy with between 15 and 20 commissioners.
Ireland and others have said they will not countenance the loss of a commissioner because of the role they play as a voice for small countries.
